sections.text: And that which is given at an unsuitable place or time or to one who is unworthy, or with disrespect or contempt - such a gift is the result of Ignorance.
Om Tat Sat is the triple designation of the Eternal Spirit, by which of old the Vedic Scriptures, the ceremonials and the sacrifices were ordained.
Therefore all acts of sacrifice, gifts and austerities, prescribed by the scriptures, are always begun by those who understand the Spirit with the word Om.

We had been discussing chapter 17, Sadhatraya Vibhaga yoga, yoga of three types of faiths. We had been learning in Bhagavad Gita that our goal in life is to find ultimate happiness. And one thing we have noticed in our life is that I only can feel happy when my mind is happy.
So the goal is to keep this mind in a happy mode. And for that I have to purify my mind, purify my mind and intellect, which is an internal instrument to achieve the ultimate goal of liberation, liberation from my limitations. Right now, the limitations which I have create sorrows and anxieties and regrets.
So to become ultimately happy, I need to get out of my limitations. These limitations exist right now because of my identification with this body, mind, and intellect. Mind is the tool I use to decide whether I am happy or unhappy.
So my first goal is to purify my mind, so it remains in a happy mode -- the Mana Prasadah. So we have seen in this chapter that as my mind, so is my personality, my faith. Bhagavan said that there is someone who has no guidance from the scriptures or from a guru, or from any wise person.
But each one of us has faith that I will achieve happiness one way or other. And then wherever my faith is that my happiness lies, those are the pursuit Ill pursue. So Arjuna asked Bhagavan, what kind of a faith is that? Bhagavan said, this faith can be of three different kinds.
This faith can be Sattvic, Rajasic, or Tamasic. Depending on your mind being Sattvic, Rajasic, or Tamasic, you will be convinced your happiness lies in those types of endeavors. So Bhagavan said: your faith, your mental texture -- as the faith, so is the person; as the person, so is the faith.
It is very important for me to understand what is making me unhappy, what makes my mind unhappy. And therefore this chapter helps us understand how Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas affect my life. So the first thing we have seen: Bhagavan said that everything you do in life will be controlled by your mental makeup -- the type of food you like, the type of food you will take, the yajnas which you perform, all the effort you put for the greater good.
But that greater good also include myself. So therefore, all my actions which I perform are basically to achieve their ultimate goal of becoming happy. So those actions which I offer as my sacrifice to get my happiness is my yajna.
See, those yajnas will be also of three different types. Sattvik, rajasik and tamasic. So we have seen that the ahara, the sattvik people will eat what is good for them.
And nutritious. Rajasic people will eat whatever is pleasant, whatever feels good. And Tamasic will take whatever is available.
Yajnas -- Sattvic people will perform without any expectations for the fruits; the Rajasic will have a goal in mind, what they want to get out of these efforts; and the Tamasic just doesnt care. Then we talked about tapas, austerities -- but in our life we call it discipline. I have to discipline myself to do this.
I was just reading this morning. Now, the new research says that not doing exercise is as bad as smoking cigarettes every day. I better be careful because Im the one who obviously does not get motivated for exercise that easily.
So now I say, oh, I need to exercise. Thats something Im telling myself. I need to perform to be in a good shape.
I want to be in good shape because I want to be healthy. I want to be healthy because that makes me happy. So ultimately, all the tapas which we do, all the disciplines which we practice, are for my happiness.
Bhagavan said Tapas is performed at three different levels: you perform at your physical level in your actions, you perform at your speech level, And you perform at the mental level. So the actions level, My actions should be helping others and not harming others. All my activities, I keep in mind that my actions are for the greater good.
Once I take care of the greater good, I am already included in it. Because any action performed by any one person in this universe affects the entire universe. We know that we are all connected with each other.
If one person in family is unhappy, it makes the whole family unhappy. So we know that that why I should be performing this for greater good. Because it ultimately will affect me if someone is suffering.
That suffering will eventually come down to me. The bhagavan said that the tapas are performed at three different levels. My activities should be such that it is for the greater good, then at the speech level, my speech should be such that it is truth but pleasant sounding truth.
All we husbands have a good idea of this. When your wife says, how do I look -- do you really want to be truthful? You can be truthful, but it has to be pleasant-sounding. Satyam Vada, Priyam Vada.
Bhagavan said your speech should be not only truthful and pleasant, but also beneficial. If I tell somebody a truth, it has to be for his or her benefit, not just because I want to be Satya Vadi Harishchandra. So thats at the speech level.
And then at the mental level -- I may be acting in a manner that looks so Sattvic, I may be speaking so softly and nicely, but if there is noise in my mind which is completely different from my actions and my speech, it will eventually affect my speech and my actions. Therefore, at the mental level, this tapas is what Bhagavan is describing. Now when Im performing, it can also be the same three categories of Sattvik, rajasic and tamasic.
Again, my tapas is for not for getting anything out of it, but it is something I need to do. So thats the purification of your internal instrument. My tapas is to purify my internal instrument so that I can experience that happiness in my mind.
And the last thing we are seeing is the Dana. Charity is our general idea is it is to help others. In reality, charity is to help yourself.
Therefore, Vivekananda said: if you find somebody who is worthy of helping, when you help, thank him for giving you the opportunity to help -- so that you can help yourself. Dhanam is for me to purify my mind and control my ego. Dana gives me the opportunity to purify my mind by giving away things which are in abundance with me.
Dana is also a social phenomenon to keep the equilibrium in society. We know that in any given society there will be income inequality. People are not born with the same resources and therefore there will be inequality.
And if I happen to be the one who is fortunate enough to have more than what I need, it becomes my duty and it becomes my means to purify my mind by doing charities. So charities are strictly for me and not for others. So when the I perform charities, I must be very clear why Im performing these charities.
So there Bhagavan said that these charities can be seen as three types. Again, Sattvik Rajasik or Tamarsic. The first one says Datavyam.
The very first requirement for appropriate Sattvic Dana, which will give you the most result of what youre looking for. What youre looking for in your life is to purify your mind to a point that it is always in a sunny, bright mood and youre always happy. You do not want to be grouchy and unhappy, complaining and regretful.
So to keep my mind in that mode, Im performing all of this -- Im eating the right food, doing the right yajna, doing the right tapas. When I do also, I have to keep in mind Im doing it for me and therefore I should know how to make these charities. So the first requirement is Datavyam Iti -- I see a cause and realize there is no other way but for me to help.
You are going on a road and you see a little child just about to get hit by a car. You dont sit down and say: is this going to be a Sattvic act or Rajasic? Is it going to be Tamasic? At that point you have no other thought than I need to help that child get him or her out of the harms way. So when you do a charity and you have that attitude, it has to be done, it has to be done then thats the right charity.
And when you give, you are not obliging that person -- actually, you should thank him: you are obliging me by giving me a chance. If theres no one to help, who are you going to help? When we were at the old temple, we were having this annadhanam, because every Sunday people would come there. But if you are feeding people who are already fed, that is not Annadhanam -- it is just a party you are having.
Every week we all get together. When a person needs food and you give him food, thats Annadhanam. If a person is already fed, you cant give him food and call it charity.
Deshe kale cha patre cha ta danam sattvikam smrutam -- when it is given at the right time, at the right place, to the right person. So if I want to help somebody and that person is sitting in a group of his friends, and I go and say: you told me that you need help -- Here is my hundred dollars which you asked for. You are insulting him in front of his friends and family.
He didnt want other people to know his problems. He came to you to ask for help, and now youre helping him at the wrong place. Wrong place, wrong time.
You should also not help somebody who you know does not need any help. Sometimes people say: I dont get a chance to do all this social work. I want to do social work, but people are not making me president of this organization.
You shouldnt worry about it. Bhagavan says Patra -- only help someone who really needs help and is seeking help. When you find that opportunity, take that opportunity that is Gods given to you.
Consider that as Gods blessing that you came across this opportunity to help that person and therefore youre helping. Bhagawan says thats a Sattvik dharam. Youre not expecting anything out of it.
Just like the example of a child in a harms way. When you help that child youre not expecting anything, not even thank you from anybody. At that point your only thought is I need to get that child out of the harms way.
Its the exact same emotion you should have when you give somebody any help: that person needs help, and I have the means -- I need to help that person. Bhagavan says thats Sattvic Dana. Yatu pratyupakarartham phalam uddishya va punah diyate pariklistam tadanam rajasam smrutam.
In contrast to that, the gift which is given in view of receiving something in return -- phalam uddishya. Ill make this donation so I can get this tax benefit. And at least people will think that he is a good donor.
I am doing these charities so it will help my business. So all companies say we are connected, we give back -- all that is actually just marketing.

These verses describe tamasic giving and introduce the sacred formula Om Tat Sat - the triple designation of the Eternal Spirit (Brahman). Tamasic dana is given adesha-kale (at the wrong place and time), apatrebhyah (to unworthy recipients), asatkrtam (without respect), and avajnatam (with contempt) - it demeans both giver and receiver. But then Krishna offers a powerful tool for transformation: Om Tat Sat - by which the Vedas, Brahmanas, and sacrifices were ordained from the beginning. Om represents the transcendental reality beyond all parts; those who understand the Spirit begin all acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity by uttering Om, remembering that all manifestation is ultimately one.
The teaching of Om is profoundly practical. Even if your faith is currently rajasic or tamasic, beginning any action with the remembrance of Om - the ultimate unity behind all diversity - can gradually purify and transform that faith toward sattva. This week, experiment with this ancient practice: before beginning any significant action (work, conversation, meal, or practice), pause and silently invoke Om, remembering that you and all beings are manifestations of one reality. Notice how this shifts your relationship to the action and to others involved. Also examine your giving: Have you ever given in a way that embarrassed the recipient or showed contempt? True giving preserves dignity and arises from respect for the Divine in the other person.
